question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q2b — Shipwreck Depth, Total Pressure, Force on Hatch (Caribbean Sea)
question.text:
A shipwreck is fully submerged at the bottom of the Caribbean Sea. The liquid pressure on the top surface of the shipwreck is 430 kPa. Atmospheric pressure = 100 kPa; density of sea water = 1025 kg m⁻³; g = 10 N kg⁻¹.

(i) Calculate the depth of the shipwreck below the surface. (4 marks)

(ii) Calculate the total pressure on the top surface of the shipwreck. (1 mark)

(iii) A hatch door on the top surface has an area of 0.60 m². Calculate the downward force on the hatch door. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q2b(i) — Depth:

Liquid pressure: P = ρgh → h = P/(ρg) = 430 000 / (1025 × 10) = 430 000 / 10 250 ≈ 41.95 m ≈ 42 m

Q2b(ii) — Total pressure:

P_total = P_atmospheric + P_liquid = 100 + 430 = 530 kPa

Q2b(iii) — Force on hatch:

F = P_total × A = 530 000 Pa × 0.60 m² = 318 000 N = 318 kN

steps.label:
Given: P_liquid = 430 kPa | P_atm = 100 kPa | ρ = 1025 kg/m³ | g = 10 N/kg | A = 0.60 m²
Formulas: P = ρgh | P_total = P_atm + P_liquid | F = P × A
Calculate the depth of the shipwreck. (4 marks)
Calculate the total pressure on the top surface. (1 mark)
Calculate the downward force on the hatch door. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Rearrange P = ρgh to get h = P / (ρg). Use P in Pa, ρ in kg/m³, g in N/kg.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Total pressure = atmospheric pressure + liquid (hydrostatic) pressure = 100 + 430 = 530 kPa.
